John Travolta: Top 10 Movies

19 March 2024 · RewindZone Archive

John Travolta's illustrious career has been a rollercoaster ride of soaring highs and challenging lows, ultimately solidifying his status as a true Hollywood icon. From his humble beginnings to becoming a household name, Travolta has captivated audiences worldwide with his magnetic charm, undeniable talent, and unwavering dedication to his craft. This article will delve into the actor's remarkable journey, exploring the pivotal roles that catapulted him to stardom and the career resurgence that cemented his enduring legacy.

Cast: John Travolta, Kyra Sedgwick, Forest Whitaker

In the 1996 drama "Phenomenon," John Travolta delivers a heartfelt and captivating performance as George Malley, an ordinary small-town mechanic who develops extraordinary mental abilities after witnessing a mysterious light in the sky. Travolta portrays George's transformation from a simple and unassuming man to a genius with a profound understanding of the world around him with sincerity and depth. He effectively conveys George's initial confusion and fear as he grapples with his newfound powers, as well as his growing sense of wonder and empathy for those around him. Travolta's nuanced and emotional performance creates a compelling and relatable character, making "Phenomenon" a touching exploration of the human condition and the power of the human spirit.

Main Cast: John Travolta, Kirstie Alley, Olympia Dukakis

Advertisement

At #9 is the heartwarming comedy Look Who's Talking, where Travolta lends his voice to the inner thoughts of a newborn baby, providing a unique and hilarious perspective on parenting. His ability to capture the innocence and curiosity of a child's mind is both endearing and entertaining, showcasing his impressive comedic timing and delivery.

Cast: John Travolta, Nancy Allen, John Lithgow

Landing at #8 is the 1981 thriller "Blow Out," John Travolta delivers a compelling performance as Jack Terry, a troubled sound technician who inadvertently records a car accident involving a political figure. Travolta masterfully portrays Jack's transformation from a B-movie sound effects specialist to a relentless investigator, skillfully conveying his character's desperation, paranoia, and determination to uncover the truth. Travolta's nuanced acting effectively captures Jack's emotional turmoil and moral dilemmas, creating a gripping and memorable portrayal that showcases his versatility as an actor.

Cast: John Travolta, Debra Winger, Scott Glenn

At #7 is Urban Cowboy, where Travolta delivers a raw and intense performance as Bud, a young Texan seeking fame and fortune in the world of honky-tonk bars and mechanical bull riding. His portrayal of blue-collar life and the struggle for identity resonates deeply, with Travolta conveying vulnerability and determination remarkably well.

Cast: John Travolta, Emma Thompson, Kathy Bates

The #6 spot goes to the political drama Primary Colors, in which Travolta delivers a powerful performance as a charming but flawed presidential candidate loosely based on Bill Clinton. His ability to capture the complexities of the character and navigate the nuances of political intrigue is truly impressive. Travolta's on-screen chemistry with co-stars Emma Thompson and Kathy Bates adds depth and authenticity to the film, making it a standout in his diverse filmography.

Cast: John Travolta, Gene Hackman, Rene Russo

Advertisement

At #5 is the delightful crime comedy Get Shorty, showcasing Travolta's versatility and impeccable comedic timing as Chili Palmer, a loan shark entangled in the world of Hollywood filmmaking. His charm and wit shine through in this role, making it a standout in his career. As an experienced movie critic, I can attest that Travolta's performance in Get Shorty is a masterclass in delivering humour with impeccable timing and nuance.

Cast: John Travolta, Nicolas Cage, Joan Allen

Claiming the #4 spot is the action-packed thriller Face/Off, where Travolta and Nicolas Cage deliver tour-de-force performances as an FBI agent and a terrorist who swap faces through a highly experimental surgery. Travolta's ability to seamlessly transition between the two vastly different characters is extraordinary, showcasing his commitment to his craft and willingness to take risks.

Cast: John Travolta, Olivia Newton-John, Stockard Channing

The iconic musical Grease lands at #3, with Travolta shining as Danny Zuko, the leather-clad heartthrob who captures the hearts of countless audiences. His electrifying dance moves and undeniable charisma make this a timeless classic that continues to resonate with generations of viewers. Travolta's performance perfectly embodies the rebellious spirit of the 1950s, and his chemistry with co-star Olivia Newton-John is simply magical.

Main Cast: John Travolta, Karen Lynn Gorney, Joseph Cali

Coming in at #2 is Travolta's breakout role as Tony Manero in Saturday Night Fever, a cultural phenomenon that has transcended generations. His mesmerizing dance moves and the iconic white suit have become ingrained in popular culture. This film not only showcased Travolta's incredible talent as a dancer but also his ability to portray a complex character struggling with issues of identity and social class. As a movie critic with 20 years of experience, I can confidently say that Travolta's performance in Saturday Night Fever is a true embodiment of the raw energy and authenticity that defines great acting.

Main Cast: John Travolta, Samuel L. Jackson, Uma Thurman

Claiming the #1 spot is the cult classic Pulp Fiction, directed by the brilliant Quentin Tarantino. Travolta's mesmerising portrayal of Vincent Vega, a smooth-talking hitman, redefined the crime genre and marked a career resurgence for the actor. His electric on-screen chemistry with co-star Samuel L. Jackson and the famous dance sequence with Uma Thurman are unforgettable moments in cinema history.

John Travolta's remarkable career has spanned decades, and his ability to embody diverse characters has solidified his status as a true Hollywood icon. From the gritty streets of Pulp Fiction to the high-energy dance floors of Saturday Night Fever and Grease, Travolta's performances have left an indelible mark on the hearts and minds of moviegoers worldwide. His versatility, commitment to his craft, and undeniable charisma have made him a true cinematic icon, and his contributions to the world of film will continue to inspire and entertain audiences for generations to come.

As my final thought, as controversial as it may be, I will offer you up a bonus pick:

Michael (1996)

Director: Nora Ephron

Starring: John Travolta, Andie MacDowell, William Hurt and Bob Hoskins

To me, it often felt that around this time, John Travolta's films were shot down and ridiculed just because he was the leading actor. Michael is definitely a testament to this theory. No, this is neither a masterpiece nor an Oscar-worthy film. It is, however, fun, charming, sentimental, and endearing. If you watch it for these reasons, I think you may be surprised!
